<!-- pr-reviewer: 62f987130943e76e59dad71ec2ed99da4e53d795 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

What looks good
- `app_icon::with_icons` sets the small icon on all platforms. It sets the taskbar icon (`ICON_BIG`) only under `#[cfg(windows)]`. The Linux and macOS code is unchanged, so the build stays portable.
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` was added. `taskbar_icon()` returns `None` and writes a `diag_warn!` line when the PNG does not decode or `Icon::from_rgba` refuses it. The window then opens with the default icon.
- The PNG files are embedded with `include_bytes!`. A missing file is a compile error, not a run-time error. A corrupt file takes the logged fallback above.
- The 256 px icon is a size of the project logotype from `assets/logo/icons/`. It is the maintainer's own artwork and `assets/ui/LICENSES.md` covers it. No new asset is added.
- No snapshot PNG changed. No `build.rs`, dependency, script or `.github` change.
- The new test pins the 256 px decode and checks that the window attributes carry the icon.

Results (locally, merged with main; no runner was used)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- app_icon`: 2 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- This machine is Windows, so the `cfg(windows)` arm was compiled and run.

Requested before merge
- None.

Questions / notes (not blocking)
- Hand check owed: nobody has looked at the icon on a Windows taskbar, title bar or Alt+Tab. The PR body says this too. This is not a blocker.
- The unit test cannot read back the `ICON_BIG` value. It checks only `window_icon`. This is acceptable.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
